relations.relation: segment filed application into its distinct required-part components (request/id, title, specification, claim(s), drawings, abstract, oath/declaration, fee submission)
determine presence or absence of each individuated required part within the application
assess whether the specification section satisfies statutory (§112-type) disclosure sufficiency
verify relative order and language conformance of present parts against prescribed filing sequence
aggregate presence, disclosure-sufficiency, and ordering outcomes into an overall completeness-and-structure determination
enumerates the distinct formal parts a complete filing must contain (request/identification, title, specification, at least one claim, drawings where applicable, abstract, oath/declaration, fees)
locates, for each enumerated required part, the corresponding section or artifact within the application
identifies textual features of the specification indicating written-description and enablement content required under §112
compares the sequence and language of the located parts against the required filing order and language convention
combines per-part presence and §112-sufficiency findings into an overall structural-completeness determination
individuates the filing into discrete structural units (request/identification, title, specification, claim(s), drawings, abstract, oath/declaration, fees)
matches individuated units against the enumerated required-parts checklist to mark each as present or absent
computes whether individuated units appear in the required sequence and in the required language
compares the presence/order findings against the minimal statutory criteria for according a filing date and admission to examination

metric.name: Application parts and formalities — completeness and structure
metric.text: Ensure the application includes all required parts in proper form (request/identification, title, §112‑compliant specification, at least one claim, drawings where required, abstract, oath/declaration, fees), in correct order/language, to secure a filing date and enter examination.
